answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a rugged canyon grid to verify geographic presence. An issuer assigns precise coordinates as a saffron anchor, and each signed receipt proves an agent occupied the site. A verifier functions like a cryptanalytic cipher tool, replaying logs to detect latency shifts; any discrepancy beyond the noise floor triggers a permanent penalty. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs to reach sites, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion.
